scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for August‑September is 88%, below the 95% target, indicating missed manual reads. This shortfall can increase reliance on estimation and contribute to billing disputes.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff modifications were logged in the billing system during the observed period.

The observation shows that among disputed bills, more have ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240), indicating that estimation shortcomings are not the primary source of disputes; issues with actual meter reads (e.g., manual read errors) likely contribute significantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This staffing shortfall can increase reliance on estimation and potentially contribute to the rise in dispute tickets.
Dispute ticket volume rose sharply to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming the stakeholder‑reported doubling since August.

Dispute response times are within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days), indicating that the surge in dispute tickets is not driven by slow response; the underlying issue likely lies elsewhere, such as incorrect bills.
